pains.label: Finding genuine projects from direct clients, without upfront fees or brokers
pains.definition: Small operators hunting for real voice or non-voice campaigns. Most offers come through middlemen or ask for upfront money. Forum posts, Quora questions and 'how to get international clients' videos.

pains.label: Fake project providers and consultants take upfront money and vanish
pains.definition: Operators who paid a consultancy or 'direct client' for a process that turned out fake, and want their money back. Includes questions about how to tell fraud projects from real ones.

pains.label: Client pays late or doesn't pay for seats already worked
pains.definition: Delayed or missing payouts from the client after the campaign ran. Chasing invoices, wanting a fixed payout, the stress of late payment.

pains.label: Outbound numbers show as 'Spam Likely' or get blocked, so nobody picks up
pains.definition: Carrier labels, Truecaller, STIR/SHAKEN and TRAI 140/160-series rules cut contact rates on outbound campaigns. Operators ask how to un-flag numbers.

pains.label: Agents keep leaving; hiring, training and absenteeism eat the margin
pains.definition: High attrition and shrinkage on the floor, first-day ghosting, the cost of replacing agents. Site heads call it a nightmare.

pains.label: Dialer trouble: dropped calls, dead air, carrier disconnects, setup and configuration
pains.definition: Technical failures on VICIdial and similar dialers that stop the floor: random disconnects, 0-second drops, agent phone not ringing, dial-plan issues, fresh setup for a new centre.

pains.label: Choosing a dialer or cloud telephony and knowing what it really costs
pains.definition: Which dialer, VoIP or cloud contact-centre software to buy in India, per-seat pricing, hidden costs, hosted versus self-hosted, whether it is worth it.

pains.label: Scoring calls and passing the client's quality audits
pains.definition: Manual call audits in Excel, agents failing QA, scorecards and metrics, hiring quality analysts, buying QA or auto-QA software so the client's audit passes.

pains.label: Clients ask for AI or a lower price per seat; AI voice agents threaten the seat model
pains.definition: Pressure to add AI voice agents or auto-QA, move to outcome-based pricing, or lose the contract. Fear that AI replaces call centres and BPO jobs.

pains.label: Setup cost, cost per seat and whether the margin is worth it
pains.definition: What it costs to set up or run a centre in India or the Philippines, seat leasing and office cost, profit per seat, pricing models, is the business still profitable.

pains.label: ISO 27001 or PCI DSS certification clients demand: cost, consultants and deadlines
pains.definition: Certification cost in India and the Philippines, which standard applies, PCI DSS v4.0 future-dated requirements and the ISO 27001:2022 transition deadline, PCI-compliant payment handling on calls.

pains.label: Licences, registrations and rule changes: OSP/DoT, TRAI DLT, PEZA, NPC/DPO, DPDP Act, TCPA consent, work-from-home limits
pains.definition: The paperwork and rules an operator must follow to run legally or keep incentives: OSP registration, TRAI DLT and telemarketing rules, PEZA registration and WFH share, NPC/DPO registration, DPDP Act readiness, US TCPA consent rules.

pains.label: Night differential, labour-law compliance and unpaid-staff accusations
pains.definition: Labour Code obligations such as night shift differential, DOLE probes into call-centre labour violations, staff left unpaid when a centre closes.

pains.label: Scam call centres tarnish the industry; clients and customers distrust offshore centres
pains.definition: Reputational damage from scam busts and fraud news, stereotypes about Indian and Filipino call centres, buyers who hate overseas support.

pains.label: Agents or fake hires steal data or money; clients demand fraud controls
pains.definition: Insider fraud, hiring fraud, data theft and social engineering inside the centre, fraud-risk assessment and prevention that clients expect.

pains.label: Missing client SLAs and paying penalties when internet or power drops or staffing falls short
pains.definition: SLA metrics and penalty clauses, internet and power outages in the Philippines, downtime communication, business continuity.

pains.label: Forecasting, scheduling and shrinkage: keeping seats filled to hit client hours
pains.definition: Workforce management software, seat utilisation, shrinkage formulas, hiring WFM and real-time analysts.

pains.label: Joining NASSCOM or CCAP to be seen by enterprise buyers: fees and paperwork
pains.definition: Industry body membership fee slabs, eligibility and application process, consultants who help get the certificate.

reasoning: Pains are drawn from the 1175 round-1 search titles. Each is a problem the operator faces, phrased the way the forum, Quora and vendor titles phrase it. Topics with no problem behind them (industry overviews, agent job guides, wrong-CCAP pages) got no pain.
